original_target.title: Sharp leading Betti coefficient for intersections of real quadrics

full_original_statement:
Fix an integer $`k\ge4`$. For each $`n\ge k`$, let
```math
B(k,n)=\max_{q_1,\ldots,q_k}
\sum_{i\ge0}\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_i(X;\mathbb F_2),
\qquad
X=\{[x]\in\mathbb {RP}^{n}:q_1(x)=\cdots=q_k(x)=0\},
```

where the maximum is over real homogeneous quadratic forms on $`\mathbb R^{n+1}`$. Singular common zero sets and dependent forms are allowed.

Is it true that, for every fixed $`k\ge4`$,
```math
B(k,n)=\frac{2^{k-2}}{(k-1)!}\,n^{k-1}
       +O_k(n^{k-2})
\qquad(n\to\infty)?
```

The homology is ordinary singular homology with coefficients in $`\mathbb F_2`$; the total Betti number of the empty set is zero. The error constant may depend on $`k`$.

sources.scope_comparison: Theorem 25 explicitly assumes generic homogeneous quadrics and gives 2^(k−2) binomial(n,k−1)+O(n^(k−2)), the desired leading coefficient in that class. Remark 23 states that removing genericity requires the slightly worse bound in Theorem 17. The target maximizes over all singular and dependent forms, so the generic theorem does not provide its upper bound. Random hypersurface arrangements concern unions or complements and graded Betti tables are different invariants. No later complete matching extremal-coefficient claim was found.
